# `Q-12-25` — Listing Id Collides With Section Id (retired)

> Older Quarto 2 releases warned when a listing's `id` was also a
> section's id; current releases render the listing as `listing-<id>`,
> so the two no longer collide.

## What this means

A heading with no explicit id gets one derived from its text, so
`## Learn more` becomes `<section id="learn-more">`. Quarto 2 releases
0.29 through 0.32 rendered a listing into an element carrying the
listing's own `id`, so a listing also called `learn-more` gave the page
two elements with that id, and Quarto warned with this code:

``` markdown
---
listing:
  - id: learn-more
    contents: posts/*.qmd
---

## Learn more

::: {#learn-more}
:::
```

Releases after 0.32 render a listing into an element whose id is
`listing-` followed by the listing's `id` — `listing-learn-more` here —
as Quarto 1 does. The section keeps `learn-more`, the listing gets its
own anchor, and this code is no longer emitted. If you see it, you are
on an older release.

The `::: {#learn-more}` slot still works as before: Quarto renders the
listing into it and gives it the new id. Links or CSS that targeted the
listing as `#learn-more` should now use `#listing-learn-more`.
